exposure: presence of anxiety and depression (screened preoperatively using Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale)
outcome: quality of recovery after caesarean delivery (measured using Obstetric Quality of Recovery-11 scale)
cohort: The study included 137 patients aged >= 18 years who underwent elective and urgent caesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia.
finding: Positive screening for both anxiety and depression before caesarean delivery was associated with a poorer quality of recovery on postoperative days 3 and 5.
